translation.text: And from there I went into another place, away from the wilderness[b]; and I drew near to the east[a] of this mountain.[c]

footnotes.text: The Geʿez expression is direction of morning or sunrise, hence east; this note applies to east rather than another place.
The term rendered wilderness can also mean desert or barren region.
Or I drew near to this mountain on the east; the placement of the directional phrase is not certain.

translation.text: And there I saw trees of judgment[a], giving off[b] the fragrance of frankincense and myrrh; and the trees also resembled nut-bearing trees[c].

footnotes.text: The printed Charles 1906 Geʿez has †ኵነኔ, judgment, marked corrupt; the printed Greek parallel likewise has κρίσεως. Charles proposes fragrant in printed page 69 notes 14 and 27. That is an editorial conjecture, not the reading printed in either main text. Judgment remains semantically difficult.

The Geʿez †ፈድፋደ is marked corrupt. Giving off follows the editor’s repair πνέοντα in printed page 69 note 28, not the printed Greek main-text πιέοντα or an unproblematic Geʿez reading. The following bracketed [ቈስቍስ፡] is untranslated: printed note 29 calls it unintelligible and an intrusion if the Greek is right, while considering a corrupt tree name.

Only the final parenthesized comparison noun (ከርካዕ።) is editor-supplied in the Geʿez with assistance from the Greek; the preceding resemblance words are printed without parentheses. Charles 1906 printed page 69 notes 18 and 29 and page 70 note 2 explain the supply. Greek καρύαις means nut-bearing trees of several kinds; almond is one proposed identification, not a proven species or independently attested Ethiopic manuscript clause. The suffix -ሂ in the selected ወዕፀወሂ is additive or emphatic, not a plural possessive their; the English therefore says the trees also. This follows the actual primary Dillmann 1865 column 2 suffixed-adverb entry, not an adoption of the Greek possessive αὐτῶν.
